title: Dreamland food, Ollie Powers and May Alix taking her job
summary: She also doubled at after-hours clubs; Bottoms ran a first-class kitchen; she worked with tenor Ollie Powers and left her job to May Alix, a stockyards worker.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now, we are now talking about -- when you were at Dreamland, what year are we talking about?
The year of Dreamland?
It was before --
Well, that was before I came to New York.
Yes. So we're still not in the '20s yet.
No. Uh-huh. No, we're not into the '20s yet.
We're getting close to it, right.

Getting very close to it, though, because when I -- when I -- while I was working at Dreamland I worked at the -- I mean, when I left Dreamland I worked at a little old club over there on Wabash. No, I don't want to bring that, because that's when I left and came right straight to New York. I worked at Dreamland, and I used to work down at the after hours clubs, too. I used to double down to the after hours clubs, to the Eden and those clubs.
Oh, yes.
Make money down there.
Did they serve food at the Dreamland?
Yes, oh, yes. Mr. Bottoms, he was a cook himself, you see. As I say, he was Joe Louis's dietician.
Right.
And the food, everything, was first class at Dreamland.
Uh-huh.
And they had to be first class. They had a guy at the door, old Jones at the door, yelling ladies and gentlemen there. And I worked with a fellow named Ollie Powers. What a voice.
He had a very high voice.
Tenor.

Yes. But what a tenor. He had one of the sweetest tenor voices you ever heard in your life. And they had a girl there named Bertha Hill, I think her name was. She had a sweet voice. Then you had May Alex She's another one used to run and do the split.
She worked with Jimmy Noone a lot.
Yeah. She worked with Jimmy Noone a lot.
Uh-huh.
May Alex You know how she got that job? She worked at the stockyards.
Uh-huh.

And she used to come in all the time, you know, as a customer. Well, when I got ready to leave the Dreamland, I told her, I said, "I'm going to New York and I'll ask Mr. Bottoms to leave you in my place." And that's how she got the job. Mr. Bottoms gave her the job when I left Dreamland. Now, I worked at Dreamland, and I'm trying to think if I didn't come back to Chicago and work at the Sunset. I don't think the Sunset was right along while I was just working regularly.
